verdict.rationale: Superset's 'prompt-first' workspace creation lets users type a natural-language task description that an agent immediately acts on (superset-docs-18), and the orchestration skill supports natural-language fan-out commands like 'split this migration into independent slices' (superset-docs-14), plus NL-ish contextual requests via the Design pane (superset-gh-1). However, broader product operation (managing workspaces, automations, projects, tasks) is primarily done via GUI, CLI, or SDK rather than free-form NL commands, and the MCP server enables agent-to-agent control rather than direct end-user NL operation. Missing for 10: evidence of NL-driven control over settings/automations/project management, and independent confirmation that NL prompts reliably drive non-coding product actions.
